hook.text: Instead of sacrificing zinc, pump electrons into the steel from an external power supply — forced protection.

buildup.text: Impressed current cathodic protection uses a rectifier to push current from inert anodes into the structure.

discovery.text: The anodes don't dissolve — they're made of titanium or graphite and last for decades.

twist.text: Excess current causes hydrogen embrittlement or coating disbondment — the protection level must be carefully controlled.

climax.text: Cross-country gas pipelines run on impressed current systems powered by solar panels in remote areas.

punchline.text: Supply electrons from outside and the metal has no reason to corrode.

quiz.question: What is a risk of over-protecting with impressed current?
options: Excess current can cause hydrogen embrittlement or coating damage
